newsitem.title: USA: Access Beyond and Hayes to merge, will keep Hayes name.
newsitem.headline: Access Beyond and Hayes to merge, will keep Hayes name.

text.p: Hayes Microcomputer Products Inc., the privately held pioneer in computer modem technology, said Wednesday that it will merge with tiny Access Beyond Inc. and become a publicly held company.
The companies said they agreed to combine in a $248 million stock transaction that will create a new company that will be called Hayes Communications Inc. and be headed by Hayes founder Dennis Hayes.

The two companies have been operating for several months under a multi-level strategic alliance agreement and the new company is expected to have annual revenues of about $277 million, the announcement said.

Access Beyond, based in Gaithersburg, Md., will issue about 45 million shares of its common stock in exchange for all outstanding shares of Hayes, leaving Hayes owners with about 79 percent of the new company's stock, which will be traded the Nasdaq market.
Based on Access Beyond's Wednesday trading price of $5.50, down 44 cents from Tuesday, the stock swap would be worth about $247.5 million.

Hayes, which is based in Norcross, Ga., said it had a commitment from a potential investor under which it will receive a $30 million cash infusion in exchange for about 12 percent of the company. Those proceeds will be used for debt reduction and working capital purposes.

The announcement said that Dennis Hayes, 47, the chairman of Hayes, will become chairman of Hayes Communications, with Access Beyond Chairman Ron Howard, 41, becoming vice chairman and executive vice president of business development.
Hayes President and Chief Executive Joseph Formichelli, 54, will assume those posts at the new company.
The transaction will be treated as a purchase for accounting purposes but is structured as a tax-free reorganization to the shareholders, the announcement said.
Hayes, which introduced the PC modem in 1981, makes and markets modems, remote access servers, cable modems and terminal adapters, as well as communications software.
The company, which emerged from bankruptcy protection last year, it is one of the largest manufacturers of modems in the world, with distributors in more than 45 countries.

"Access Beyond's family of high-quality, low-cost remote access solutions, including recently introduced technologies for Microsoft Windows NT servers, coupled with Hayes' brand name recognition in the computer communications industry, state-of-the-art manufacturing capabilities and full service multi-channel sales, marketing and distribution network, creates a formidable company with tremendous growth potential," the companies said.
